name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: CVE-2026-102764 — BeyondTrust Remote Support Authentication Bypass by Spoofing Vulnerability
items.dek: BeyondTrust Remote Support. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 19 October.

items.title: CVE-2025-61624 — Fortinet Multiple Products Path Traversal Vulnerability
items.dek: Fortinet Multiple Products. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 19 October.

items.title: My Credentials, Please: Detecting Filesystem Capability Laundering in MCP Servers at Scale
items.dek: 16.4% of MCP servers expose filesystem capabilities beyond their declared contract; dynamic evaluation confirms 150 exploitable instances across registries.
items.unproven: whether the vulnerability manifests in production deployments where agents run with restricted filesystem permissions by policy or container isolation

items.title: Language Is a Security Surface for Agent Guards
items.dek: Agent safety guards shift verdicts on translated requests; smaller and purpose-built models flip decisions beyond noise floor, with flips rising to +4.4pp on rare languages.
items.unproven: whether the effect propagates to code-switching or hybrid requests, or whether guard vendors have since addressed language-dependent brittleness

items.title: Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations
items.dek: Evaluation datasets for agent safety guards contain dataset shortcuts predicting labels; guard performance degrades sharply under domain holdout or balanced weighting.
items.unproven: whether the audit framework detects shortcuts in newly released benchmarks, or whether disclosed findings have prompted benchmark redesign

items.title: Big Fish: Exploiting a 37-Year-Old Kernel Bug in OpenBSD
items.dek: 37-year-old OpenBSD kernel bug exploited; demonstrates longevity of undetected memory safety issues in privileged code.
items.unproven: Scope limited to OpenBSD; does not establish prevalence in other kernels or whether similar patterns persist in reader's deployment targets.

items.title: Prompt injection in HTTP headers: what 217M web responses show
items.dek: Study of 217M web responses shows prompt injection patterns in HTTP headers; corpus-based measurement of known attack class.
items.unproven: HTTP header injection prevalence does not establish exploitation risk in the reader's SDLC context; survey-scale finding

items.title: Superconducting circuits host two-level systems with lifetimes exceeding one second
items.dek: Two-level systems in superconducting circuits exhibit lifetimes exceeding one second, orders of magnitude longer than host qubits.
items.unproven: characterization on one qubit type; unclear whether these TLSs are controllable or can be harnessed rather than merely understood.

items.title: BiShield-TEE: On the (In-)Security of Unilateral Weight Obfuscation in On-Device TEE-Shielded LLM Partition
items.dek: Unilateral weight obfuscation in TEE-shielded on-device LLM inference is broken by Solution Determinacy Property; bilateral obfuscation proposed as fix.
items.unproven: whether bilateral obfuscation withstands cryptographic attack or is itself vulnerable; evaluation is limited to GroupCover and ArrowCloak without real-world deployment testing

items.title: I never authorized an integration that scans my secrets
items.dek: GitHub's secret-scanning integration enrolls repositories without explicit user consent, raising audit and compliance questions.
items.unproven: whether the reader's own org has been affected; scope of exposure across customer base

items.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
items.dek: LLM-guided evolutionary search discovers quantum circuits reducing Toffoli and qubit counts in seven of eight tasks, including a new reversible modular-inversion architecture.
items.unproven: quantum-algorithm optimization; entirely outside application security engineering remit

items.title: Magna: simulating magic state factories as cheaply as Clifford circuits
items.dek: Magna simulator classically evaluates magic-state factories and distillation protocols by expressing them as tensor networks without exponential cost growth.
items.unproven: quantum-circuit simulation tool; entirely outside application security engineering remit

items.title: Private Retrieval Augmented Generation via Random Projection
items.dek: Random projection preserves RAG retrieval quality while mitigating data extraction attacks, outperforming formal differential privacy baselines empirically.
items.unproven: whether the privacy gains hold against adaptive attackers with knowledge of the projection scheme, or scale beyond the tested datasets and architectures

items.title: Realization Divergence in Multi-Provider Quantum Computing: A Pre-Registered Study of What Survives Measurement
items.dek: Realization divergence across three quantum vendors shows placement policies affect two-qubit overhead and execution ordering; pre-registered study.
items.unproven: eight- and twelve-qubit circuits on current NISQ devices; no evidence that this measurement framework or divergence metrics inform secure design choices

items.title: Encoded but Exposed: Language Embeddings can Reveal More Than They Should in Recommender Systems
items.dek: Item embeddings in recommender systems leak identities via cosine similarity when adversaries hold auxiliary item text; leakage persists through semantic alignment.
items.unproven: whether obfuscation mitigations are practical under production performance constraints, or whether the attack applies to proprietary commercial embedding models

items.title: Smoothness of Shortest Isogenies to Frobenius Conjugates
items.dek: Smoothness of shortest isogenies to Frobenius conjugates validates p^(1/3+o(1)) unconditional attack on supersingular endomorphism ring problem.
items.unproven: post-quantum cryptography adoption timeline; whether this affects ML-KEM or other NIST-approved KEM implementations the reader will deploy

items.title: Stability of Quantum LDPC States under Local Pauli Noise
items.dek: Conditional mutual information decay in qLDPC code projectors under local Pauli noise exhibits exponential stability across weak and strong noise regimes.
items.unproven: quantum error correction theory; entirely outside application security engineering remit

items.title: Magic in quantum trajectory unravelings of noisy random quantum circuits
items.dek: Magic content in quantum-trajectory unravelings of noisy random circuits depends on Kraus-operator choice independent of observable expectation values.
items.unproven: quantum resource theory; entirely outside application security engineering remit

items.title: Subgraph Counting with Local Node Differential Privacy
items.dek: Optimal algorithms for subgraph counting under local node differential privacy achieve O(n^(k−1/2)/ε^(k−1)) error with matching lower bounds.
items.unproven: applicability to the reader's domain; this is theoretical computer science with no connection to application security, SDLC tooling, or agent deployment

items.title: SynDebug: A Framework to Debug Logic Bugs in Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Programs
items.dek: Framework for debugging fault-tolerant quantum programs with minimal overhead; quantum computing is distant from current SDLC integration.
items.unproven: only quantum simulators tested; production quantum hardware deployment remains years away

items.title: Patchwork: automated lattice surgery and space-time partitioning for real-time decoding
items.dek: Lattice surgery compiler for surface-code quantum error correction with automated scheduling.
items.unproven: post-quantum cryptography migration; not yet demonstrated on deployed systems or realistic noise

items.title: SMT-Boosted Security Types and Correctness for Low-Level MPC
items.dek: SMT-based type theory and Hoare logic enforce correctness and confidentiality in secure multi-party computation protocols automatically.
items.unproven: this addresses MPC language verification, not application security engineering; relevance to the reader's SAST/DAST/SCA tooling and SDLC process is absent

items.title: Jianmu-Q: Bridging Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Hardware with AI Agents
items.dek: Multi-agent framework translates quantum field theory descriptions into quantum simulation workflows; validated on three field theories.
items.unproven: tested only on three specific field theories in noiseless simulation; no evidence the approach generalizes or scales to production quantum hardware workflows outside physics research.

items.title: ZZ-Free bSWAP Gates under Strong Driving in Far-Detuned Fixed-Frequency Transmons
items.dek: 150-ns gate operation on far-detuned transmons using XX-YY interaction; 33% faster SWAP than cross-resonance.
items.unproven: demonstrated on one qubit pair; no evidence this transfers to multi-qubit processors or improves end-to-end algorithm performance.

items.title: Synergistic charging of a quantum battery via Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and non-Markovian noise
items.dek: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya coupling and non-Markovian noise jointly enhance quantum battery charging in two-spin systems.
items.unproven: toy systems only; no experimental validation or scaling evidence for practical quantum batteries.

noise.title: OpenCode Hacked: User credentials leaked
noise.dek: Credential breach at OpenCode reported via social media; no technical detail, scope, or remediation path given.
noise.unproven: identity of affected users, nature of credentials, whether the reader's org uses OpenCode, timeline, or mitigation steps

noise.title: Israeli firm's digital ads enabling installation of 'zero-click' spyware
noise.dek: Zero-click spyware via ads attributed to Israeli firm; news coverage of known threat with no new technical detail.
noise.unproven: high HN engagement does not indicate new method or exploitation vector

noise.title: Zero-Click Spyware Delivered via Targeted Ads: AdFection
noise.dek: Citizen Lab documents AdFection zero-click spyware delivery through targeted ads; known threat group with established technique.
noise.unproven: incident report; no new SDLC-level defense or detection method emerges from documentation
